verdicts.reason: A keeps the original's hierarchy: a large italic quote, a small gold attribution, and the can sitting in the circle at bottom right. The can and circle are a bit small, and the left side below the attribution is empty. B inverts the hierarchy: the quote is shrunk to body-text size while the attribution is far bigger, the quote text runs onto the edge of the circle, and the logo has moved to the top as a competing focal point.

A shrinks the quote to tiny text with an orphaned 'soon.' on its second line, makes the attribution dominate the quote, and lets the text straddle the circle's edge. B keeps the original's large two-line quote, its type hierarchy and the can-in-circle composition. B's only flaws are minor: the can is slightly small and there is some dead space at the lower left.

A reduces the quote to a small single line and makes the attribution bigger than the message. The text also sits over the edge of the circle, and the can is pulled out of the circle that framed it. B faithfully keeps the large quote, the subordinate attribution and the can within the circle. Only minor polish is needed on B, such as the empty lower-left area.

A keeps the original's structure and type hierarchy cleanly. B shrinks the quote to small text under a much bigger attribution and jams the text block at the top. The can hangs half over the circle's edge, the logo is isolated at the bottom centre, and there is a large dead area between them.
